correctness.rationale: The signature permits only direct multiplication atoms on e,x,y, not nested product terms. Independently enumerated all 9 equality and 27 ternary atoms on pointed pairs for cyclic, elementary abelian and nonabelian Heisenberg groups. The proof reduces the entire diagram to x=e,y=e,x=y,x^2=e,y^2=e,x^2=y,y^2=x,xy=e. For each fixed nonidentity x the exceptional y values are e,x for p=2; e,x,x^{-1} for p=3; and e,x,x^2,x^{-1},x^{(p+1)/2} for p>=5, whose pairwise distinctness and p>=7 generic residue yield exact one-step extension sets independent of commutativity. Two-round EF equivalence is equality of the possible pointed extension profiles from both sides, producing six classes. Rank<=2 separating sentences prove they are distinct; only the exponent-3 nontrivial-noncyclic class requires minimum size 9. The independent finite atomic signature calibration found exactly six classes including H3,H5, and does not replace the all-finite-groups lemmas.

originality.rationale: Gomaa 2007 Chapter 3 (the same ternary relation with a named identity) proves EF-depth and variable bounds for finite abelian groups and cyclic prime groups; full primary chapter inspected. A Resultary predecessor improves binary closure estimates for prime cyclic EF distinguishing depth, but does not state the six rank-two theories across all prime exponents, including nonabelian groups. Existing group WL algorithms use a stronger subgroup-generation or pebble language. This theorem restricts quantifier nesting sharply to two with relational, not function-symbol multiplication; textbook atomic-type ideas alone do not give the six-class cross-prime census without the exceptional-response proof.

value.rationale: Exact quantifier-rank-two theory census in a natural relational group signature answers how much low-depth logic detects prime-exponent structure, including nonabelian groups. Complete finite canonical representatives and sharp nine-point minimum representative bound have independent interest for descriptive complexity and logical model comparison.

final_claim: In first-order equality language with named e and ternary relational multiplication R(x,y,z) iff xy=z, every finite nontrivial group with prime exponent belongs to exactly one of six quantifier-rank<=2 theories, represented by C2, C2^2, C3, C3^2, C5, C7. The largest minimum representative order is 9. Class C7 also includes all prime exponent>=7 and exponent-5 groups of size>5, including nonabelian groups.
limitations: Equivalent two-variable/low-depth group theory census in older finite-model-theory literature may exist under type spectrum terminology.
